explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: $2.77/hr index (+1.8% 7d) Oct 2 print, flat on Oct 1 and at the Sep 30-Oct 1 highs; H200 $3.37 (+2.1% 7d); MI300X $2.63 (+0.4%); A100 $1.58 (+0.6%); RunPod H100 SXM $3.49/$2.69, Lambda $3.99-4.29 (last checked Sep 30); Nebius H100 list +17% live from Oct 1; CME futures not listing Oct 5 (CFTC review to Nov 9)
indicators.why: This is the marginal clearing price of installed AI compute and the most direct public read on whether capacity is being discounted; it is published daily, and a CME-listed futures contract on it is pending (CFTC review extended to Nov 9, 2026).
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if the Silicon Data H100 index holds below ~$2.00/hr for a month, if spot trades below the one-year contract rate (inversion), or if the CME H100 curve lists in steep (>15%) backwardation; the Oct-2025 trough of $1.70 is the floor to remember.
indicators.note: Oct 2: Silicon Data's SDH100RT held at $2.77, unchanged from Oct 1, so the run of daily highs paused at a plateau; the 7-day change eased to +1.8% from +4.9% as the Sep 25-28 base rolled off. H200 $3.37 (+2.1% 7d), MI300X $2.63 (+0.4%) and A100 $1.58 (+0.6%) are all unchanged on the day. Nebius's 17% H100 list rise has been live since Oct 1. Nothing new on the visibility leg: no CME/Silicon Data futures this week (CFTC review to Nov 9). Still the one contract-vs-spot marker on file is Tencent's reported ~$7B, five-year lease of ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs from Oracle in Southeast Asia (about $1.60/GPU-hr at full utilisation, chip model undisclosed) against $2.77 on-demand. RunPod and Lambda list prices were not rechecked on Oct 2.

indicators.name: B200 / Blackwell rental price, $/GPU-hour (on-demand)
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 $5.86 (+0.2% 7d) Oct 2, unchanged on Oct 1; B300 $6.70 (+1.5% 7d), down from $6.78 on Oct 1; B200/H100 ~2.12x; RunPod B200 $5.98/$6.79, B300 $6.94/$7.89, Lambda B200 $6.69-6.99 (last checked Sep 30); Nebius B200 +19%, B300 +21% live from Oct 1; CoreWeave running Vera Rubin NVL72 in production (Sep 30)
indicators.why: Blackwell is where new supply lands, so this is the first place a glut would show; if B200 rates fell toward H100 rates while Rubin ships, capacity would be outrunning demand.
indicators.watch: Bearish if tier-1 neocloud B200 on-demand drops below ~$4.50/hr, if the B200/H100 price ratio compresses below ~2x, or if lead times for 8-GPU Blackwell nodes fall to same-week availability.
indicators.note: Oct 2: the B200 index was unchanged at $5.86 (+0.2% 7d) and B300 slipped to $6.70 from $6.78 (the 7-day change reads +1.5%). With H100 at $2.77 the B200/H100 ratio is 2.12x, same as Oct 1 and above the 2x flip line; B200 sits well above the $4.50 trigger. Silicon Data's own commentary on the B200 page still describes a supply-constrained market where large labs lock up multi-year reserved capacity and absorb most Blackwell supply. Rubin is shipping (CoreWeave Vera Rubin NVL72 in production) and Blackwell spot has not softened into it. RunPod and Lambda list prices were not rechecked on Oct 2.

indicators.name: Legacy-GPU residual value: used H100 prices, A100/H100 rates and booked useful lives
indicators.value: A100 index $1.58/hr (+0.6% 7d) Oct 2, unchanged, above the $1.50 trigger; used H100 SXM ~$18-27K by age vs $30K list (Jun); Reuters: lenders underwrite GPUs on 3-4 yr schedules vs Nvidia's 'up to a decade', want more than 25% residual guarantees on the $500B financing plan; Amazon reportedly putting ~$8B of Grace Blackwell chips in a financing vehicle, source notes ~5-yr chip replacement cycle; MSFT/Meta lives unchanged
indicators.why: Depreciation is the biggest cost in a GPU cloud; if old chips still earn money the 5-6 year accounting lives hold and no write-downs are coming, whereas collapsing used-H100 prices would be the first hard evidence of oversupply.
indicators.watch: Bearish if 8-GPU H100 servers trade below ~50% of new-build cost on the secondary market, if A100/H100 rental rates fall below ~$1.50/hr, or if any hyperscaler extends server lives beyond 6 years to flatter earnings; also watch for Hopper impairments at neoclouds.
indicators.note: Oct 2: A100 index flat at $1.58 (+0.6% 7d), H100 $2.77 and H200 $3.37 unchanged, so the rental side of residual value is intact. New on the lender side: Bloomberg, relayed by Techzine, reports Amazon is exploring a special-purpose vehicle holding about $8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips across 12+ US data centers, issuing debt and selling up to 10% of equity, with Amazon leasing the hardware back; an investment-grade rating is the aim so pensions and insurers can buy in. The article flags the catch for investors: advanced chips have a replacement cycle of about five years. That sits alongside Wednesday's Reuters survey (banks underwrite 3-4 years, want stronger guarantees and IG customers behind Nvidia's $500B plan): chips are now being financed as collateral, and the market is pricing their lives conservatively. No new used-H100 prints, impairments or useful-life changes found.

indicators.name: All-in AI data-center build cost, $ per GW (with GPUs / ex-GPUs)
indicators.value: ~$47B/GW Vera Rubin (≈$32B racks + ≈$15B shell/power/cooling); ~$60B/GW gas-powered campus (Orennia); Project Jupiter $165B for 2.45 GW ≈ $67B/GW all-in; TCS Hyderabad $7.4B for 1 GW ex-GPU shell; CDC Gregadoo (Wagga Wagga) A$15B ≈ US$10B for a 'gigawatt-scale' ex-GPU campus, concept phase
indicators.why: Cost per GW sets the revenue a campus must earn per GPU-hour to clear its cost of capital; rising cost means supply is constrained (good for rental prices) but raises the bar for returns and the size of the debt stack.
indicators.watch: Discounting signal if Nvidia rack ASPs or $/GW start falling (Nvidia gross margin guided below ~72%, rack prices cut) while rental $/hr does not rise; bubble-risk signal if ex-GPU cost (power, shell, turbines) keeps inflating faster than rental rates.
indicators.note: One datapoint added, and it is Australian: Infratil-backed CDC Data Centres is planning a A$15B, gigawatt-scale campus at Gregadoo outside Wagga Wagga (ABC Sep 29; Region Riverina and BeBeez Sep 30). CDC's own site calls it 'concept phase', transmission-level grid connection, closed-loop cooling, no capacity or timeline disclosed. At roughly US$10B for about a GW of shell, power and cooling it sits between TCS Hyderabad (~$7.4B/GW) and the ~$15B/GW US ex-GPU figure - consistent with regional-Australian land and power being cheaper than Texas, not with costs falling. Prior datapoints unchanged: Oracle's Project Jupiter ($165B for 2.45 GW, ~$67B/GW, force majeure Sep 24) and the Orennia $60B/GW gas-campus benchmark. Memory input costs still rising (see memory_prices).

indicators.name: Server DRAM / HBM contract price momentum (QoQ) and DRAM spot
indicators.value: Micron FQ4 (Sep 30): rev $54.23B vs $51.5B est, non-GAAP GM 87.0%, DRAM ASP +high-teens QoQ, NAND ASP ~+30%; FQ1 guide $61.5B ±$1.5B at ~86.25% GM ('low point for FY27'); 'vast majority' of CY2027 HBM bits contracted at significantly higher YoY prices; supply-constrained through 2028; MU -3.1% Thu 10:30 ET on the beat; TrendForce 2027 HBM ASP +121%; DDR5 16Gb spot $58.00 (Oct 2, +0.12%), DDR4 16Gb $83.59 (-0.09%); Tesla halves AI5 LPDDR5 to 72GB as memory tightens
indicators.why: Memory is the tightest physical input to AI servers (HBM is 25-30% of a Rubin rack) and contract prices are negotiated quarterly, so this is the earliest cyclical input to turn; a price rollover would precede GPU discounting.
indicators.watch: Bearish when server DRAM or HBM contract prices go negative QoQ, when 2027 HBM4 contracts are signed at lower prices, or when DRAMeXchange DDR5 spot falls >20% from peak; also watch whether CSPs start cutting memory per system (TrendForce now says GPU makers are evaluating 8-Hi instead of 12-Hi HBM stacks), which is the buyers' cost response. Near term: Samsung Q3 prelim Oct 8 (consensus cut to ~107T won); TrendForce 4Q26 contract settlement; Micron's FQ1 print in December against an 86.25% guide it calls the FY27 low.
indicators.note: Oct 2 DRAM spot (18:10 Taipei): DDR5 16Gb $58.00 (+0.12%), DDR4 16Gb $83.588 (-0.09%), DDR4 8Gb $46.321 flat - a sixth session of sub-0.2% moves, so spot has plateaued at the high while contract keeps stepping up. Two buyer-response datapoints today, both the demand side adapting to scarce memory rather than prices cracking. Tesla is cutting memory per chip: AI5 LPDDR5 from ~144GB to 72GB and AI6 LPDDR6 by about a third to 144GB, to secure volume for Optimus and cut cost; Musk says the performance hit is 'negligible' because bandwidth, not capacity, is the constraint (TrendForce, citing Musk, Wccftech, Seoul Economic Daily). That is the 'CSPs cut memory per system' line in the watch field showing up at one large buyer. Storage is tight too: Toshiba is spending $380M to double AI-data-center HDD capacity by FY2027, with Seagate's nearline capacity said to be allocated through 2028 (TrendForce). Samsung's Q3 prelim is expected Oct 8 with Korean press now around 105T won operating profit. Micron sold off 3.1% Thursday on the beat (stockanalysis.com) - the sold-the-news read, as an 87% gross margin and $61.5B guide were already priced; the Friday move was not checked. Contract-side unchanged: TrendForce 2027 HBM ASP +121% YoY.

indicators.name: Power constraint: ERCOT interconnection queue, gas-turbine backlog and lead times
indicators.value: 474 GW ERCOT queue (~90% data centers); Texas TCEQ permit freeze since Sep 21, compliance report due Oct 19; BNEF: 49.8 GW delayed; GE Vernova 116 GW backlog, ~20 GW/yr output, new orders land ~2030-31; Oracle force majeure on 2.45 GW Project Jupiter (gas pipeline to Feb 2027); US Senate blocks Ratepayer Protection Act 57-43 (Sep 30); Dover DE 18-month and Dixon CA 45-day data-center moratoria
indicators.why: Power, not chips, is now the binding constraint on new capacity, which keeps installed GPUs scarce and rental prices firm; it also reveals how much announced demand is speculative once regulators force projects to prove financing.
indicators.watch: ERCOT files its Batch Zero eligibility-verification and community-impact reports by Dec 10, 2026 for the Dec 17 PUCT open meeting, with RFIs going out Aug-Sep and cure periods Oct-Nov: large queue withdrawals (BNEF flags 49.8 GW at risk) would show phantom demand. Turbine slot cancellations or resales, falling data-center PPA prices, or turbine prices retreating from the $600/kW 2027 forecast would signal the build is slowing. Nearer: TCEQ compliance report Oct 19, Project Jupiter air-permit decision Nov 23.
indicators.note: No new queue, turbine or permit numbers on Oct 1; the Texas freeze stands with TCEQ's report due Oct 19 and ERCOT's audit still targeted for mid-December. The only addition is another local pause: Dixon, California approved a 45-day moratorium on new data-center approvals to study water, power and infrastructure impacts (ABC10, Sep 30), joining Dover, Delaware's 18-month pause - small towns, but the pattern of pre-emptive closures is what turns a queue into phantom demand. What moved Sep 30 was the politics of who pays for power. The US Senate failed 57-43 (60 needed) to advance Sen. Husted's Ratepayer Protection Act, which would have made state regulators decide whether data centers bear the incremental cost of grid build-out; the House had passed it 417-3 on Sep 16, and Democrats blocked it as 'toothless', pushing a GRID Savings Act that would make data centers pay full upgrade costs (KSL/AP, Sep 30). Either version raises the ex-GPU cost of a campus; neither passed, so the status quo holds for now, but both parties are now campaigning on making data centers pay. Prior items unchanged: Oracle's Sep 24 force majeure on Project Jupiter (gas pipeline to Feb 1, 2027, air permit Nov 23); GE Vernova 116 GW backlog against ~20 GW/yr output; Exelon's ~40% cut to 'high-probability' data-center load.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capex vs cloud backlog (RPO) growth, and capex as % of cloud revenue
indicators.value: Anthropic prospectus: $518B of compute commitments over 7-10 yrs (Broadcom leases $161.2B, Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, xAI/Nvidia up to $84.5B, Microsoft $31.4B, AMD $20B+), ~80% non-cancelable; Anthropic pre-IPO investor session Oct 14, formal marketing week of Nov 9; Amazon expects ~$220B 2026 capex and is exploring an $8B off-balance-sheet chip vehicle; Oracle RPO $664B plus reported $7B/5-yr Tencent GPU lease, but force majeure on Project Jupiter; Micron ~$150B RPO, H1 FY27 capex ~$25B; Goldman: US hyperscaler capex $1.4T in 2027
indicators.why: Capex is the supply side and RPO is the contracted demand side; as long as backlog grows faster than capex the build is pre-sold, but capex above 100% of cloud revenue with negative free cash flow means the cycle is now funded by debt and equity and is sensitive to any demand wobble.
indicators.watch: Bearish if RPO growth decelerates below capex growth for two quarters, if 2027 capex consensus (+57% per Morgan Stanley) gets cut or 'digestion' language appears, or if backlog concentration in a few AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) produces a cancellation or renegotiation; Oracle's Project Jupiter force majeure is the first payment-deferral mechanism triggered on a Stargate site - watch whether it spreads.
indicators.note: Oct 2 adds two items on how the build is being funded and one on timing. Amazon: Bloomberg, relaying the FT, says it is exploring an SPV for about $8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips across 12+ US data centers, selling debt and up to 10% of equity and leasing the hardware back; the stated driver is $220B of 2026 capex, mostly AI, and it keeps the hardware off the balance sheet (Techzine). Anthropic: Bloomberg (via Yahoo) reports a pre-IPO session for select institutions at its San Francisco HQ on Oct 14, with formal marketing now expected the week of Nov 9 and a potential November listing at a $1.8-2T valuation under discussion - so the mid-October roadshow in earlier reports has slipped about three weeks. The $518B commitment stack (~80% non-cancelable) and its ~$60B of related chip financing (see neocloud_credit) stand. Prior ledger unchanged: Oracle's $664B RPO with Tencent's reported $7B lease and Project Jupiter force majeure, Micron's ~$150B RPO and ~$25B H1 capex. The counter-signal is the same: capex is outrunning cloud revenue, so more of it is being financed off balance sheet and in private credit. Next hard data: TSMC Oct 15, then late-October hyperscaler prints.

indicators.name: Neocloud financing: CoreWeave loan/bond spreads, CDS, vendor backstops, customer concentration
indicators.value: Broadcom-led ~$60B AI-chip financing for Anthropic and others: $42B senior-secured Class A (bank syndicate) + $18B junior Class B led by Blackstone ($9B own capital), pricing undisclosed (Bloomberg, Oct 2); Amazon exploring ~$8B Nvidia-chip SPV, IG rating the aim; CoreWeave $4.2B 2.875% converts (Sep 24); Lambda $926M TLB at SOFR+300, Baa2 (Sep 22); CoreWeave loans still ~SOFR+550, debt $35.1B at Jun 30; GMI Cloud $668M (Oct 1); lenders want >25% residual guarantees and IG-customer backing on Nvidia's $500B plan; data-center ABS $11.9B YTD vs $15.5B in 2025; CRWV $91.25 (+3.0%) at 10:29 ET Oct 2, 52-wk $60.55-153.20
indicators.why: Neoclouds are the levered marginal builder of GPU capacity; their cost of debt, covenants and dependence on Nvidia backstops show whether lenders still believe rental prices will cover depreciation, and they are the first place a compute-price decline turns into forced selling.
indicators.watch: Escalation if new deals price above SOFR+600 or 11% yields, CDS above 1,000bp, deals pulled or downsized, Nvidia's rent-back backstop extended to tier-1 neoclouds, or a top customer (CoreWeave's A/B/C are 36%/26%/10% of revenue) renegotiates; improvement if spreads retrace toward the April 9.75% level or if CoreWeave can tap convertible/equity-linked money on Nebius-like terms.
indicators.note: Oct 2 is a financing-volume day. Bloomberg reports Broadcom and a bank syndicate are assembling about $60B to fund AI chips for Anthropic and other customers: a $42B senior-secured Class A tranche for syndication and an $18B Class B junior tranche led by Blackstone, which is putting in $9B of its own capital; it is separate from Broadcom's own $42B lending commitment to Anthropic disclosed in the prospectus. Pricing and collateral were not disclosed, so there is no spread read. The shape is the point: a junior tranche that needs a private-credit anchor means the senior lenders want a cushion beneath them, the same demand for subordination and guarantees Reuters found on Nvidia's $500B plan. Amazon's reported $8B SPV (see hopper_residual) targets an investment-grade rating. CRWV was $91.25, +3.0% at 10:29 ET Friday (stockanalysis.com), ~40% off the $153.20 high; its Fully Connected launches and the expanded Nvidia partnership are the stated drivers, and no new CoreWeave debt print or CDS level was found today. Signal stays neutral: capital is available at very large size, but it is arriving in tranches that price in downside, anchored to contracted rental streams rather than to the chip.

indicators.name: Nvidia data-center revenue growth, gross margin and customer concentration
indicators.value: DC rev $89.0B +117% YoY (Q2 FY27), GM 75.0%, Q3 guide $108B at 74%; one direct customer >=10% (16%); five customers = 70% of receivables; supply commitments $279B; OpenAI Ohio backstop cut to <$120B; $150B buyback added Sep 28 ($235B remaining); $500B chip-collateral financing plan (Blackstone/Apollo/KKR) meeting lender pushback; Broadcom-led ~$60B chip financing and Amazon's ~$8B Nvidia-chip SPV show rivals and customers building their own financing; Tencent reportedly leasing ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs via Oracle SE Asia ($7B/5 yr)
indicators.why: Nvidia's margin is the purest read on whether GPUs are being discounted at the source, and its concentration plus growing vendor-financing (backstops, campus guarantees) shows how much of demand is circular.
indicators.watch: Bearish if gross margin is guided below ~72% for more than one quarter, data-center revenue grows <5% sequentially, three-customer concentration exceeds 60% in the 10-Q, DSO climbs past 60 days, or backstop commitments expand beyond the $108.5B disclosed; Q3 FY27 report due ~Nov 2026.
indicators.note: Operating figures unchanged from the Aug 26 10-Q and the Sep 28 buyback. Oct 2 read-throughs are about financing, not volume. Amazon is reportedly moving about $8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips into an SPV with external debt and equity, so a top customer is already syndicating the chips it bought (Techzine, via Bloomberg/FT). Broadcom and its banks are lining up about $60B to fund Anthropic and others, a vendor-finance play modelled on Nvidia's (Bloomberg via Yahoo). Both come as lenders push back on Nvidia's own $500B collateralised plan (3-4 year underwriting vs 'up to a decade', >25% residual guarantees, IG customers). Net: demand for Nvidia silicon is still being financed, but the financing is increasingly done by others and on stricter terms, which weakens the circularity point in the 'why' at the margin. Demand and cost lines from Oct 1 stand: Tencent's $7B Oracle lease of ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs (a line Washington could cut), Micron's HBM4E foundry base die and 2027 HBM priced 'significantly higher' against a 74% Q3 guide. Rubin revenue is live (CoreWeave Vera Rubin NVL72 in production). No public forward curve (CFTC review to Nov 9). Next data: Q3 FY27 print ~Nov.
